title: Moving zeros of a restricted linear series outside a fixed cluster
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a nonempty projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $V\subseteq H^0(X,L)$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-linear subspace, where $H^0$ means global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and let $\Gamma$ be an irreducible component with its reduced closed-subscheme structure [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Write $L|_\Gamma$ for tensor restriction [def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume $\dim_k\operatorname{im}(V\to H^0(\Gamma,L|_\Gamma))\ge2$. Let $Z\subseteq X$ be a zero-dimensional closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. There are finitely many proper $k$-linear subspaces $W_1,\ldots,W_t\subsetneq V$, including $\{0\}$ among them, such that for every $s\in V\setminus\bigcup_iW_i$ there is a closed point $x\in\Gamma\setminus|Z|$ at which $s$ vanishes. Vanishing means that the image of the germ $s_x$ in the one-dimensional residue-field vector space $L_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)$ is zero [def-weil-residue-field]. Thus the exceptional set is contained in a finite union of proper linear subspaces; its complement is a nonempty Zariski open of the affine space $V$ in any basis.

source.place: Tag 0B40 (lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial), with the normalization and fixed-divisor corollary formulated by the worker; moving-point input serving Franciosi--Tenni Lemma 3.3 Step 1, printed p.236, and Lemma 3.2. The corollary is not claimed verbatim in Stacks.

proof.text: The reduced component $\Gamma$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme], and has dimension one by pure dimensionality. Compose its closed immersion in $X$ with the given projective embedding of $X$; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] makes $\Gamma$ H-projective over $k$; it is also quasi-compact, being closed in the quasi-compact $\mathbf P^N_k$, so $\Gamma$ is projective in the convention of [lem-pc-projective-proper], hence proper (in particular separated and of finite type) by that node. The normalization $\nu:C\to\Gamma$ is finite, surjective and birational, with $C$ a smooth proper integral curve, by [lem-sc-normalization-properties]. Here $k$ is perfect: in positive characteristic each element has a $p$th root because $k$ is algebraically closed. Let $M=\nu^*(L|_\Gamma)$. This is invertible, since tensor pullback of each local rank-one trivialization is again a rank-one trivialization.

source.place: Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic); normalization of an integral curve, followed by smoothness over the perfect field

proof.text: Let $\rho:V\to H^0(C,M)$ be restriction followed by pullback and put $U=\operatorname{im}\rho$. Pullback $H^0(\Gamma,L|_\Gamma)\to H^0(C,M)$ is injective: a section pulling back to zero is zero at the generic point by birationality; on every affine trivialization its coefficient lies in a domain and injects into that domain's fraction field, so is zero. Consequently $U$ is finite-dimensional and $\dim_k U\ge2$. By [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite], $Z$ is finite over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], its support is a finite set of closed points, and $T=\nu^{-1}(|Z|\cap\Gamma)$ is finite and consists of closed points of $C$.

source.place: Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0); the section injection is the affine domain calculation

proof.text:
$C$ is a smooth connected curve over $k$: it is nonempty, connected and one-dimensional by Step 1, of finite type over $k$ because $
u$ is finite and $\Gamma$ is of finite type, and separated because $
u$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres](1) and $\Gamma$ is. Apply [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] to $C$: it is Noetherian and integral, its closed-point rings are discrete valuation rings, and its generic local ring is a field, so all local rings are regular. The divisor calculus [lem-pc-regular-curve-divisor-calculus](2) associates to every nonzero $u\in U$ an effective divisor $D_u$ and an isomorphism $\mathcal O_C(D_u)\simeq M$. By the degree homomorphism of [def-sc-pic0], every such divisor has the same integer degree $d=\deg[M]=\sum_P\operatorname{ord}_P(u)$. Since $U
e0$, $d\ge0$. There are only finitely many effective divisors supported on $T$ with degree $d$: each coefficient is an integer between $0$ and $d$. Denote by $\mathcal E$ this finite set; it is allowed to be empty.

source.place: Tags 0BE8 (lemma-normal-c1-injective), 0BE9 (lemma-local-rings-UFD-c1-bijective); compare varieties.tex Tag 0B40 and its effective-divisor proof

proof.text: For each $D\in\mathcal E$ realized as $D_u$ for some $0\ne u\in U$, choose one such $u_D$. If $D_v=D_u$ then the rational function $v/u$ has order zero at every closed point. In the local generators of [lem-pc-regular-curve-divisor-calculus], both $v/u$ and its inverse lie in every local ring. Equivalently the valuation definition of $\mathcal O_C(0)$ and $\mathcal O_C(0)=\mathcal O_C$ in clause (1) give global sections of $\mathcal O_C$. By [lem-sc-global-functions], $v/u\in k^*$. Conversely nonzero scalar multiples have the same divisor. Thus the nonzero sections realizing $D$ form exactly $k^*u_D$, and $\ell_D=ku_D\subset U$ is a line.

source.place: Tag 0BE8 proof: order-zero rational functions are units; varieties.tex Tag 0BUG (lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections)

proof.text: Take as exceptional subspaces $\ker\rho$, all $\rho^{-1}(\ell_D)$ for the realized $D\in\mathcal E$, and $\{0\}$. They are linear subspaces and proper: $\rho$ surjects onto $U$, which has dimension at least two, while $\ell_D$ has dimension one. If $s$ lies outside them, $u=\rho(s)\ne0$ and $D_u$ is not supported on $T$, since otherwise $D_u\in\mathcal E$ and $s\in\rho^{-1}(\ell_{D_u})$. Thus some closed point $y\notin T$ has $\operatorname{ord}_y(u)>0$, which means that $u$ vanishes in the residue fibre at $y$ by the local uniformizer description.

source.place: Tags 0BE8, 0BE9: elementary assembly of the divisor classification and the surjective linear map

proof.text:
Put $x=
u(y)$, viewed also as a point of $X$. It is closed because $
u$ is finite and hence closed [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], and $\Gamma$ is closed in $X$. It lies outside $|Z|$ since $y
otin T$. In a local frame of $L$ at $x$, the fibre value of $u$ at $y$ is the image of the coefficient of $s$ under the field injection $\kappa(x)	o\kappa(y)$. Its being zero forces that coefficient to be zero in $\kappa(x)$. This is precisely the required vanishing of $s$ at $x$.

source.place: Tag 02OR (lemma-zero-scheme): residue-fibre vanishing; explicit local coefficient calculation under pullback

proof.text: In any basis of $V$, a linear subspace is the common zero set of finitely many linear forms, so the complement of this finite union is Zariski open. It is nonempty by [lem-pc-finite-linear-avoidance]. Its infinite-field hypothesis holds: if $k$ were finite, the nonconstant polynomial $1+\prod_{a\in k}(t-a)$ would have no root in $k$, contrary to algebraic closedness. This proves also the final affine-space assertion.
